counterhypotheses.claim: Physical single-execution serialization plus provider idempotency is sufficient; caller-bound generation capabilities add no safety benefit.
counterhypotheses.support: Production paths may continuously retain a physical gate; many providers support idempotent requests.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Frank fresh-main permits unbound/stale callers into COMMITTING; distributed systems literature uses fencing values specifically to reject delayed old writers.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Run matched B1/B2/B3 stale-caller + ABA + crash/timeout-after-acceptance matrix with (A) physical gate+idempotency only and (B) immutable caller-bound generation fence. Compare duplicate/provider-attempt safety, recovery and overhead.

counterhypotheses.claim: Structural IFC/taint labels fully solve indirect prompt injection and provenance problems.
counterhypotheses.support: CaMeL/Fides demonstrate deterministic policy enforcement for important classes.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: NeuroTaint argues semantic transformation and persistent influence can escape traditional taint abstractions; AgentSys reduces exposure by context isolation rather than labels alone.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Adversarial web->memory->later-action tests with paraphrase/semantic transformation under structural labels only vs labels+isolation+semantic provenance audit.

counterhypotheses.claim: Semantic retrieval + summarization is enough; execution-state trees/event logs are unnecessary complexity.
counterhypotheses.support: Simple RAG is cheaper and broadly applicable.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: MAGE reports better long-horizon success and lower token use than semantic-memory baselines; ESAA shows replay/audit benefits from event sourcing.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Same long-horizon corpus and failures: semantic-RAG-only vs execution-state-path+semantic memory. Measure task success, stale-state errors, recovery, tokens, DB I/O and repair locality.

counterhypotheses.claim: Deeper recurrence monotonically improves reasoning and should run until a fixed high budget.
counterhypotheses.support: Multiple recurrent-depth systems gain accuracy with extra compute.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Adaptive allocation achieves equal quality with less compute; Parcae exposes stability requirements; When Shallow Wins shows depth/correctness non-monotonicity and silent failures.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Fixed-shallow vs fixed-deep vs adaptive-stop on matched seeds; report outcome, calibration, state-delta/residual-pressure, loop regime, latency and tokens.

counterhypotheses.claim: Explicit GWT is unnecessary; equivalent recurrent/shared-memory information flow yields the same utility.
counterhypotheses.support: Structured partner models can emerge in generic recurrent agents when task pressure requires them.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Shared workspace and cross-modal global-workspace studies show gains over specific ablations.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Matched topology/control tasks: explicit candidate competition+broadcast vs shared recurrent memory vs simple cross-attention; lesion receiver-use/re-entry while preserving parameter and information budgets.

counterhypotheses.claim: Pairwise graphs are sufficient; higher-order Hyperposition adds representational and runtime overhead without outcome gain.
counterhypotheses.support: Many tasks remain solvable with pairwise graphs; HKVM-RAG shows structured support does not always convert to answer-F1.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Multiple 2026 hypergraph systems beat matched pairwise baselines on higher-order tasks.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Detect candidate irreducible interaction sets; compare pairwise, factorized and hyperedge variants at identical evidence/compute. Promote hyperedges only if utility gain exceeds overhead.

counterhypotheses.claim: A simple transactional SQLite schema with explicit versions and checkpoints is sufficient; append-only event sourcing/projections are over-engineering.
counterhypotheses.support: Frank v0.1 is a single target instance and may not need distributed-system complexity.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Current effect/identity/recovery requirements need replay, causal provenance and stale-generation rejection; event-sourced agent designs provide direct precedent.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Replay/crash/rebuild benchmark on identical workloads: normalized mutable state vs append-only events+snapshots+projections. Measure correctness, recovery time, storage amplification, write latency and query latency.

counterhypotheses.claim: ClayCode-specific typed cognition is not needed for reliability; ordinary typed host-language structs and schema-constrained calls are simpler and equally safe.
counterhypotheses.support: Structured tool schemas and direct hidden-state routing can work without a custom language runtime.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Typed workflow and DSL studies show compliance/reasoning benefits in bounded settings; project owner fixes ClayCode-only cognition as target premise.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Within owner-fixed ClayCode target, compare lowering/runtime implementations: full typed semantic IR vs minimal schema facade on identical semantics. Measure caught authority/type errors, execution correctness, compiler/runtime complexity and latency.

counterhypotheses.claim: Reactive-only agents are safer and equally useful; proactive self-generated goals mostly create drift/livelock.
counterhypotheses.support: Long-horizon autonomous systems exhibit semantic livelock and goal drift risks.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Persistent hierarchical goals and goal-evolving agents improve bounded long-horizon tasks; owner-fixed target requires proactive substrate.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Reactive vs bounded-proactive matched workload with admitted goal checkpoints. Score useful verified outcomes, user interruption compliance, idle correctness, livelock, token/tool cost and false self-reward.
